claims.statement: Fifty million dollars... Everyone who has told this story agrees on that number.
claims.evidence: Randolph, Hastings and Antioco (LinkedIn Dec 2021: 'apparently offered to sell their company for $50 million') all name $50M. Narration says Netflix 'named its price', not a firm sale offer. Unchanged since round 1.

claims.statement: Netflix, worth hundreds of billions of dollars.
claims.evidence: Market cap about $293B mid-Oct 2026; 'hundreds of billions' is the conservative wording.

claims.statement: Down to one last store, a franchised Blockbuster in Bend, Oregon.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia Blockbuster: one franchised store remains, Bend, Oregon.

claims.statement: Blockbuster was born in Dallas in nineteen eighty-five.
claims.evidence: First store 19 Oct 1985, Dallas.

claims.statement: Close to five billion dollars a year in revenue; up about eleven percent; $50M about one percent of yearly revenue.
Thousands of stores.
claims.evidence: FY2001 10-K implies ~7,677 stores (6,254 company-operated) at end 2000.

claims.statement: Parent company Viacom; whether Antioco could have bought Netflix alone is unknown.
claims.evidence: Viacom parent 1994-2004; correctly framed as unknown.

claims.statement: Around twenty years at Seven-Eleven, then ran Circle K and later Taco Bell, before he took the top job at Blockbuster in nineteen ninety-seven.
claims.evidence: Round-1 fix applied. Wikipedia: 7-Eleven 1970-1990, Pearle Vision (1990), Circle K president/CEO 1991-96, Taco Bell CEO 1996-97, Blockbuster CEO July 1997. Omitting Pearle Vision is a simplification, not misleading.

claims.statement: Hastings and Randolph founded Netflix in 1997 in Scotts Valley.
claims.evidence: Prospectus: incorporated Aug 1997; Scotts Valley per Wikipedia Netflix.

claims.statement: Meeting at Blockbuster's Dallas HQ; Hastings, Randolph and finance chief Barry McCarthy.
claims.evidence: Variety 2025 via Stratrix: everyone agrees on a Dallas HQ meeting; Randolph's memoir names McCarthy.

claims.statement: Flat monthly subscription since September 1999.
claims.evidence: Prospectus: subscription service launched September 1999.

claims.statement: ~25M US households with a DVD player by end of following year, nearly double; $21B on renting and buying videos.
claims.evidence: Prospectus (Adams Media Research): ~25M at end 2001, +91%; $21B in 2001.

claims.statement: About 300,000 subscribers; revenue $35.9M; net loss $57.4M (2000).
claims.evidence: Prospectus FY2000: revenue $35,894K, net loss $57,363K, 292K subscribers.

claims.statement: You would be paying fifty million dollars for a business on its way to losing more than fifty million dollars that year.
claims.evidence: Round-1 fix applied; no hindsight slip. Full-year 2000 net loss $57.4M > $50M.

claims.statement: In two thousand, the dot-com bubble peaked and began to burst.
claims.evidence: Round-1 fix applied; claim c54 added to research (s14). Nasdaq/dot-com peak 10 Mar 2000, followed by the decline; true for any month of 2000, so it is robust to the disputed meeting date (c14).

claims.statement: About one percent of yearly revenue; about nine hundred times the fifty million.
In his 2019 book That Will Never Work, he recalls Antioco struggling not to laugh.
claims.evidence: Vanity Fair excerpt Sept 2019; attributed as Randolph's recollection.

claims.statement: In 2023, he wrote on Twitter that Blockbuster 'laughed us out of the room.'
claims.evidence: Fortune 14 Apr 2023: 'laughed us out of the room,' Randolph recalled on Twitter. Flagged as his memory.

claims.statement: Antioco on LinkedIn (2021): 'I can say with complete confidence that there were never any serious acquisition talks in 2000.' Not part of the meeting, only greeted the guests.
claims.evidence: Verbatim per LinkedIn post 23 Dec 2021 (quoted in Stratrix; opening line visible on LinkedIn).

claims.statement: Hastings has reportedly said he doesn't think it was serious; more curiosity.
claims.evidence: Variety Mar 2025 via Stratrix; hedged with 'reportedly' and paraphrased.

claims.statement: Almost everything else is disputed. Even the month.
claims.evidence: Early 2000 (Hastings) vs Sept 2000 (Randolph/Wikipedia). Script uses 'two thousand'.

claims.statement: In May two thousand and two, it went public. $15 a share, $82.5M raised, ~$310M valuation, about six times $50M.
claims.evidence: Round-1 fix applied. Trading began 23 May 2002 (closing 29 May). Prospectus: 5.5M shares x $15 = $82.5M; 20,648,074 shares x $15 = $309.7M; 6.2x.

claims.statement: More than 600,000 subscribers (about double), more than 11,500 titles, $19.95 a month.
claims.evidence: Prospectus figures; 603K vs 292K = 2.07x.

claims.statement: Peak in 2004: 9,094 stores.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia citing SEC.

claims.statement: In 2004 it split from Viacom and launched Blockbuster Online.
claims.evidence: Spin-off Oct 2004; NBC May 2005: 'Last year, Blockbuster spent more than $200 million to launch its own mail-order online service' (re-read this round).

claims.statement: In January 2005 it dropped most late fees.
claims.evidence: Blockbuster 2005 10-Q: end of late fees from 1 Jan 2005 at US company-operated stores.

claims.statement: 2005 net loss $588M, more than half a write-down.
claims.evidence: FY2006 release: 2005 net loss $588.1M incl. $341.9M impairment (58%).

claims.statement: By then, Carl Icahn had built a stake of nearly ten percent, and in May 2005 he won a seat on the board.
claims.evidence: Round-1 fix applied. NBC 10 May 2005 (re-read): shareholder vote 'electing Icahn and two other dissident candidates to the company's board'; Icahn 'owns nearly 10 percent'. 13D/A: buying from 11 Nov 2004, 9.70% of Class A by Apr 2005.

claims.statement: Autumn 2006, Total Access: rent online, return to a store and swap for free.
claims.evidence: Release 27 Feb 2007: launched ~five months earlier; in-store exchange for free rentals.

claims.statement: ~2.2M online subscribers, 700,000 added in Q4; back in profit, $54.7M.
claims.evidence: Release 27 Feb 2007; operating income $79.1M also positive.

claims.statement: Antioco says Total Access brought Netflix back to the table and serious talks began in early 2007. That is his account.
claims.evidence: Round-1 fix applied: unverifiable 'Nobody else has confirmed it' removed. Attributed to Antioco (LinkedIn Pulse June 2022 via Stratrix).

claims.statement: Bonus $2.28M offered vs $7.65M claimed; March settlement; lump-sum exit payment just under $5M instead of $13.5M.
claims.evidence: 8-K 19 Mar 2007: lump sum $4.9875M vs $13.5M; 'lump-sum' wording now precise.

claims.statement: Antioco left; Jim Keyes CEO that same year.
claims.evidence: Release 2 Jul 2007: Keyes appointed Chairman and CEO.

claims.statement: In 2007 Netflix started streaming.
claims.evidence: Watch Now launched Jan 2007.

claims.statement: 23 September 2010, Chapter 11.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia Blockbuster.

claims.statement: Dish bought it in 2011 with ~1,700 stores; last company-owned stores closed early 2014.
claims.evidence: Wikipedia Blockbuster.

claims.statement: 2025 revenue $45.2B.
claims.evidence: Netflix Q4 2025 letter.

claims.statement: When a small company could one day replace your core business, don't only ask what it's worth today; ask what it would cost you if it wins.
claims.evidence: Round-1 fix applied: one lesson only. No factual claims.

notes: Round 2. All 7 round-1 issues are fixed correctly in script.md (IPO date, Icahn timing and board seat, removal of the unverifiable negative, the hindsight slip in c50, dot-com wording plus new claim c54, Antioco career sequence, single lesson). The optional polish was applied too ('wrote on Twitter', 'lump-sum exit payment'). Re-opened this round: NBC 10 May 2005 (Icahn elected to the board, nearly 10% stake; Blockbuster Online launched 2004). The other claims are unchanged and were verified in round 1. Structure: cold open, scene, pressure (fairness), freeze at ~44% ('Would you sign?'), reveal with all three accounts hedged, aftermath numbers, verdict line 'Blockbuster passed', one lesson. ~1,540 words / ~9:20. Non-blocking housekeeping for @researcher: the research.md claims table still lists c10 as '29 May 2002' (closing date; trading began 23 May) and c33 as 'unverified, 2005'. Updating them would keep the dossier consistent with the script, but this does not affect the narration.
